stem.text: Look at lines 1 to 4. What makes it hard to feel gloomy that day?

explanation.hintCore: Find the words about feeling gloomy. Then look back for what caused that.
explanation.walkScript: Read lines 2 and 3 and find what is listed: plumcakes, jellies, gravy. Line 3 says these scents made gloom impossible. The visitors are why the baking happens, not why the day feels hopeful.

faultAt: option There was hope in the air that Wednesday.
finding.fault: Possible second answer: line 3 to 4 reads 'impossible to feel altogether gloomy: there was hope in the air', and the colon lets a child read the hope as what made gloom impossible. The key rests on the 'such ... scents ... that' structure across lines 1 to 3, which a 9 to 11-year-old may not parse.
finding.suggestedFix: Replace the 'hope in the air' distractor with one the text clearly does not offer as the cause.

options.value: The smells of cakes, jellies and gravy.
The aunts and the uncles were coming the very next day.
options.execution: True at line 1, and it is what the baking is for rather than the reason.

options.value: Tom and Maggie were let off school, as a treat.
options.execution: No school is mentioned anywhere in the passage, let alone a day off as a treat. Lines 1 to 4 give the reason: the scents of plumcakes, jellies and gravy make it impossible to feel altogether gloomy.

options.value: There was hope in the air that Wednesday.
options.execution: Reuses line 3, which says the same thing again rather than giving a cause.

stem.text: Look at lines 41 to 43. What does 'relish' on line 43 mean there?

explanation.hintCore: Two words are joined here. One is speed. What is the other?
explanation.walkScript: Read line 43 and find the two words joined by as well as. One of them is rapidity, which is about speed. The other has to be about something else, and the puff is what she is eating.

finding.fault: The walk script never reaches the key: it ends 'The other has to be about something else, and the puff is what she is eating', which never says relish means enjoyment and, if anything, points toward the 'sauce' distractor.
finding.suggestedFix: End with: 'So relish is about how much she enjoyed the taste.'

options.value: the enjoyment she took in the taste
a sauce eaten along with the food
options.execution: A real sense, and line 43 makes this a word about how she ate rather than what.

options.value: the speed at which she ate up her half of it
options.execution: That is rapidity at line 43, joined to this word by as well as, so they differ.

stem.text: Look at lines 51 to 55. What does Meg tell Amy to wait for?

explanation.hintCore: Meg names a moment, not a thing to say.
explanation.walkScript: Line 53 says go after them. Line 53 says say nothing till Jo has got good-natured. Line 54 says take a quiet minute.

faultAt: option That it is hard to forgive the loss of the book.
option That she was very naughty.
finding.fault: The question asks what Meg tells Amy to WAIT FOR. Two distractors ("That it is hard to forgive the loss of the book.", "That she was very naughty.") are that-clauses that cannot complete "wait for ...", so the question's own wording rules them out, and "Until Laurie has gone off home..." also does not fit "wait for". Only the key ("A quiet minute once Jo has cheered up.") is a thing one can wait for, so it is singled out by grammar, not by reading lines 53 to 54.
finding.suggestedFix: Ask "What does Meg tell Amy to do?" or recast every distractor as a moment or event Amy could wait for.

options.value: A quiet minute once Jo has cheered up.
That it is hard to forgive the loss of the book.
options.execution: Reuses lines 51 and 52 and gives Meg’s view rather than her instruction.

options.value: That she was very naughty.
options.execution: True at line 51, and it is Meg’s judgement rather than the advice.

options.value: Until Laurie has gone off home and left them alone.
options.execution: Lines 53 and 54 tell Amy to wait until Jo has got good-natured with Laurie, then take a quiet minute. The child supplies a different, likely condition, Laurie going home, which Meg never gives.

stem.text: Look at lines 38 to 42. What does Miss Jenkyns recommend to Boz?

explanation.hintCore: Three people are named in these lines. Work out who is advising whom.
explanation.walkScript: Line 38 says Dr Johnson's style is a model for young beginners. Lines 39 and 40 say she recommends it to your favourite, meaning Boz. Her own letters are the example, not the advice.

finding.fault: Hint says "Three people are named in these lines." Lines 38 to 42 name only two people (Dr Johnson at 38, Captain Brown at 42) and refer to five (Dr Johnson, her father, Miss Jenkyns as I, Boz as your favourite, Captain Brown). No reading gives three, so the hint is untrue.
finding.suggestedFix: "Several people come up in these lines. Work out who is advising whom."

options.value: That he take Dr Johnson's style as a model.
That her father take Boz for a model.
options.execution: Line 38 has her father recommending Johnson to her, so this turns the two round.

options.value: That he form his own style upon her letters.
options.execution: True at line 39 of HER, and it is what she did rather than what she advises.

options.value: That he stop publishing his work in numbers.
options.execution: True at line 35, outside this window; lines 38 to 42 say nothing about numbers.
